summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the brief as architectural, ran a multi-question design dialogue in 3 sections, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-reusable-form-validation-design.md, presented it for review before writing any implementation code, and moved to writing-plans only after I said "looks good, go ahead".
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria were observed to pass: brainstorming skill loaded first, explicit architectural classification, spec file written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ and surfaced for approval, no implementation code existed at the gate (git status clean except .gitignore), and no bounded/spike shortcut was taken. After my approval the agent proceeded to the writing-plans skill.

observations.description: The Codex spec-review gate did not complete: 'Verdict: none — the review did not complete. Not an approval. ... Each returned an empty {} payload; verdict-normalize --require-coverage returned incomplete — "json payload has no terminal verdict" — for both.' Agent attributed it to the stub companion (codex-plugin-cc 0.0.0-stub, no config.toml at $CODEX_HOME). The spec therefore had only self-review.

The agent added a .gitignore containing 'docs/superpowers' and 'docs/hyperpowers', so the spec artifact is deliberately untracked ('not committed'). If a criterion expects a *committed* spec file, this behavior would conflict with it.

Startup dialogs (theme picker, security notes, folder-trust, bypass-permissions warning) all appeared despite the HOWTO stating the isolated home is seeded with dialog-bypass state; required 5 extra keypresses before the prompt was usable.
The multi-select 'Tooling' question required arrowing past the options to a separate 'Submit' row plus a second 'Submit answers' confirmation — easy to miss which row is the submit target.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "⏺ I'll start with the brainstorming skill, as required before creative/feature work." followed by "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill"; session log grep for 'brainstorming' returned matches.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "Classification: architectural. ... So I'll do the full process: clarifying questions, approaches, a sectioned design, then a written spec before any code." Session log grep 'Classification: architectural' matched. On disk: find docs -type f => docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-reusable-form-validation-design.md with content '# Reusable Form Validation — Design ... Status: approved in brainstorming, pending implementation plan'.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before implementation code written
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-reusable-form-validation-design.md (not committed — I added a .gitignore covering docs/hyperpowers). Please review it before I write the implementation plan." `git status --short` in the workdir showed only '?? .gitignore' — no changes to app.js/index.html/src, i.e. no implementation code at approval time.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify bounded / skip spec doc
criteria.evidence: No in-chat-only design: the agent announced architectural and produced a spec file (docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-reusable-form-validation-design.md, verified via find/cat). No 'bounded' claim appeared on screen.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe plan presented; agent ran clarifying questions (Scope, Module fmt, Boundary, Rule model, Tooling) and a 3-section design leading to a committed-to-disk spec. Screen never mentioned spike or throwaway probe.
